title: Regression Storm Response Playbook
content:
Purpose
This playbook captures a compact, battle-tested approach for "regression storms" — periods where multiple perf alerts fire across models or routes. It focuses on fast triage, reproducible bisects, and pragmatic rollback/mitigation so product traffic stays healthy while engineering investigates root cause.

Scope
- Applies to: hosted API + Dedicated serving runtime.
- Focus areas: alert triage, dashboard checks, bisect experiments, lightweight profiling, and canary comparison hygiene.
- Not covered in depth: long-term capacity planning, billing reconciliations.

High-level triage timeline (first 60 minutes)
1) 0–5m: Safety & ownership
   - Acknowledge alert in #eng-runtime-alerts.
   - Assign primary owner (pager) and scribe.
   - If impact > 5% of production qps, page SRE on-call.
2) 5–20m: Fast signal sweep (dashboard checklist below)
   - Confirm whether this is: single-model, single-route, or global.
   - Capture a short incident timeline (timestamps of first alert, spikes).
3) 20–40m: Bisect & canary checks
   - Run lightweight bisect plan (see bisect patterns).
   - Compare canary vs prod snapshots (metric diffs).
4) 40–60m: Mitigation or rollback
   - If root cause unclear and customer impact high, trigger rollback to last known-good model/container image.
   - Apply targeted rate-limits or route-scaling guardrails as stopgap.

Dashboard checklist (quick queries & panels to open)
- Traffic & error surface
  - total_qps: redwood.serving.requests.count (1m).
  - error_rate: redwood.serving.requests.errors / requests.
- Latency distribution by route/model
  - p50/p95/p99 token latency and request latency (redwood.serving.latency.*).
- Throughput & batching
  - tokens_per_sec, avg_batch_size, batch_wait_ms.
- Resource pressure
  - GPU_utilization, GPU_memory_used, CPU_iowait, host_memory_free.
- Scheduling & queues
  - runtime.request_queue_length, scheduler.pending_tasks.
- KV cache hit/miss ratio (for prefix caching regressions)
  - kv_cache.hits / kv_cache.requests.
- Recent deploys & canary traffic split history
  - deploy.timestamp, canary.traffic_pct, rollout.events.

Fast heuristics (is it code, model, infra, or data?)
- Code: sudden correlated latency across many routes using same runtime image or library version, matches deploy timestamp.
- Model: regressions scoped to a model id or variant; often accompanied by changed tokenization stats or longer decode times.
- Infra: elevated GPU memory pressure, host-level OOMs, scheduling backlog; may affect multiple tenants.
- Data: spike in long input sequences or malformed inputs; check recent client-side changes and sample payloads.

Bisect patterns (choose one based on scope)
- Canary split regression (fast):
  1) Compare canary vs prod metric snapshots over the last 30m.
  2) If canary shows regression, immediately scale canary to 0% traffic and revert deploy pipeline.
- Binary deploy bisect (one model/image per deploy):
  1) Identify the first deploy timestamp where the delta appears.
  2) Iteratively revert commits between last-good and first-bad in a staging harness until reproducing locally.
- Configuration/flag bisect:
  1) Snapshot runtime flags (autobatching, quantization profile, kernel override) from coordinator.
  2) Toggle suspect flag in a small canary and observe.
- Input-driven bisect (data):
  1) Collect representative failing inputs (sample 50 requests).
  2) Replay against baseline image / model in perf-lab harness.

Repro lab checklist (when you need deterministic benchmarks)
- Use perf-harness v2 with identical sequence length distribution and tokenization seed.
- Pin GPU type, CUDA/cuDNN, and container image. Note these in the experiment meta: gpu_type, cuda_version, image_sha.
- Run batches of 1000 synthetic requests; capture p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU flamegraphs.
- Save artifacts to S3 under s3://redwood-perf/experiments/YYYYMMDD-handle/ with a README.

Profiling quick recipes
- Lightweight tracing (first pass): enable 1% sampled RPC traces and look for increased request wall time in the runtime exec span.
- CPU flamegraph: perf record + FlameGraph scripts on the inference worker (sampled at 1000Hz).
- GPU kernels: capture nsight-sys short-run or ncu launch on a duplicated workload. Look for changed kernel choice or increased kernel runtime.
- Memory allocator: inspect jemalloc stats or tcmalloc fragmentation metrics; sudden growth in RSS without matching allocation pattern points to leak or fragmentation.
- KV cache diagnostics: instrument kv_cache.latency, per-key lifetime distribution, and eviction churn.

Common regression root causes and quick checks
- New fused kernel path selected (kernel mismatch): check compilation logs and kernel selection metadata stored with model artifact.
- Quantization profile regression: compare quantization matrix diffs; run a small eval set for quality/perf tradeoff.
- Batching change: confirm automatic batcher settings (max_batch_size, max_latency_ms) and effective avg_batch_size change.
- Tokenization or model input distribution shift: compute mean sequence length and token types for the last 24h vs baseline.

Mitigation actions (ordered by speed & reversibility)
1) Toggle slow feature flags (e.g., disable kernel X / revert quantization profile).
2) Reduce canary traffic or pause rollout.
3) Temporary autoscale up for affected SKU to buy time.
4) Rollback to previous model image (document image_sha and timestamp).
5) Apply per-route rate limits or degrade to smaller model variant if supported.

Communication & post-incident hygiene
- Immediately update #eng-runtime-alerts with short status updates every 15m during active triage.
- After mitigation, owner drafts a 1–2 page incident timeline with: what happened, impact, root cause hypothesis, mitigation steps, and follow-ups. Link to experiment artifacts.
- Required follow-ups: 1) cause-proof (benchmarks + trace evidence), 2) alert tuning to reduce noise, 3) automation to detect the same signal earlier.

Playbook recipes (copy-paste snippets)
- Grafana quick query for p95 latency delta across models (fill dashboard vars):
  - query: delta(redwood.serving.latency_p95{env=~"$env"}, 5m)
- Simple replay harness command (perf-harness):
  - ./perf-harness --model-id $MODEL --image $IMAGE_SHA --profile tokens.json --concurrency 8 --out artifacts/$RUN_TAG
- Flamegraph capture (Linux host):
  - sudo perf record -F 997 -a -g -- sleep 60; sudo perf script | ./FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl | ./FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl > cpu-flame.svg

Unresolved questions to investigate (examples to file as follow-ups)
- Are there subtle kernel selection heuristics that change with minor CUDA driver versions?
- Can our canary snapshot comparisons be automated to trigger a rollback on >X% regression?
- Do we need a tokenization-variance alert (rapid shift in mean length per route)?

Quick reference: Who to call
- eng-serving-runtime on-call: @eng-runtime-oncall (Slack)
- SRE escalation: @sre-oncall
- Model infra: priya.desai@redwood.example

Appendix: short incident template (paste into a new doc)
- Incident title:
- Start time / end time:
- Owner / scribe:
- Impact summary (routes affected, % of qps/users):
- Short timeline (key timestamps):
- Quick dashboard links (screenshots, panels):
- Root cause hypothesis:
- Evidence (benchmarks, traces, flamegraphs): s3://redwood-perf/experiments/XXXX
- Mitigation steps taken:
- Follow-ups and owners:

Notes to self (working observations)
- Keep reproductions as small and deterministic as possible; avoid folding in upstream CI changes.
- Prefer rolling back model image over fiddly flag changes when uncertain.
- When in doubt, widen sampling on traces rather than adding longer-running profiling to prod.
